title: Elziabeth Berkley's Performance in Showgirls is one of the best of the 90's

commenti.body:
The director has been on the record for years that he coaxed her line deliveries out of her. Her acting style on Saved By the Bell was so radically different and you can tell in other roles that she is actually very committed to the work. 

I love love love that Goldie Hawn hated the blowback reaction so much that she got her cast in The First Wives Club in 1996 just to get her another role.
It is unfortunate that she was directed to be that way by Verhoeven, but her only reward for her commitment was the loss of her subsequent career. A captivating performance to be sure.

This is a joke, right? All life on the screen actually dies when she's in frame. It's highly doubtful, it would have been a good movie with another female lead, but it's safe to say that her performance made an already doomed project bomb completely. She's just an awful, awful actress, which is probably the reason she never had a career to speak of.
[removed]

The revisionist history with this movie is absolutely staggering. I just don't understand people bending over backwards to convince themselves that this trash heap is good. I've been similar comments about Belly.

There’s a review of Chatterbox, the 1977 movie about a woman with a talking vagina, that talks about how hard star Candy Rialson is working: “There’s something actually quite moving watching her try so hard in a role that is killing her career with every minute of screen time.”
[removed]
[removed]

It’s definitely unfortunate that Showgirls probably halted any potential of her being a leading actress in any major projects, but she did remain a working actress which is all most actors can really hope for. Looking at her filmography she had at least 1 acting role every year since Showgirls except between 2017-2019. 

It’s a shame though as I think she would have shined in more comedic roles.
It's reassessment, not revisionist history. Nobody is denying that critics panned the movie in 1995.
It’s still shit even after a reassessment. Pretending it’s not is the revisionism.

I dunno, man, I enjoy myself immensely every time I watch it, and find that the movie comes up frequently and fondly in discussions with friends. 

By the way, do you like doggy chow?

> I enjoy myself immensely every time I watch it

Yeah, but people weren't wanking when they saw it in theatres, hence the more accurate assessment then.

Why is wankless film-watching somehow more accurate?

mm I love doggy chow

[removed]
I don't have to bend over backwards, it's easy to defend and there are loads of very well expressed analyses explaining its worth.

I actually thought the classic "I'm so excited! I'm so excited! I'm so scared" scene from Saved by the Bell was very well acted by her, despite how silly the actual dialogue was. She was pretty good at her job.

I saw Elizabeth Berkeley in a show in Boston with Richard Dreyfus. 2004? I actually saw her during rehearsals when she went to Whole Foods. There was so much buzz and I loved her as a kid. That I can’t even remember the name of the play is a testament to how boring everyone was. Bad. Sly Fox! Is that right? I didn’t realize how many people still own watches until 45 minutes in, I start seeing hands start popping up. I finally realize, “Oh I’m in a dud. These people want to leave.” When I saw her at market, I couldn’t believe how beautiful she was. Jaw dropping. Onstage, yeah… she’s not great. I’ve got a cast iron stomach for acting. I finished Suddenly Susan and Caroline in the City… I give actors a chance. Don’t judge. But in Sly Fox it was like watching a robot mixed with 1997 Madonna. Everyone knew about Showgirls and kept hoping. But the acting wasn’t there. I’m talking bad. Block this from your memory. The only thing I remember from the performance other than the disaster, was that she gave a better performance than Pia Zadora would have given. 20 years later, I’m not even sure about that. I’m talking an hour in, people started praying for John Wilkes Booth. But when I Met Elizabeth she was devastatingly gorgeous. So🥴

I actually saw it at the theater when it came out and kinda loved it. Yeah it was ridiculous and even gross in some parts, but that weird mix of this bright-eyed dream story combined with over the top vulgarity seemed perfect for the Vegas setting. Plus I was a Prince fan and he had some new songs in the movie. Girl 6 would make an odd bookend to it a year later, I loved that one even more.
